evidence.claim: The Manuscript Type Matches the Venue’s Aims and Scope
evidence.excerpt: "Field Notes Journal publishes research and practice-grounded writing on information systems, digital transformation, supply chain and operations management, analytics, and the use of AI in organizations. We welcome empirical studies, case studies, practitioner reports and reflective field notes that connect evidence from real organizations to theory or to practical lessons. Work should be clearly written for both academic and practitioner readers. Purely technical computer science papers without an organizational angle, and work outside business and management, are out of scope."

evidence.claim: The Manuscript Type Matches the Venue’s Aims and Scope
evidence.excerpt: Firms A and B kept one familiar spreadsheet report, rebuilt from system data, for the first quarter. Staff could compare old and new numbers side by side and raise questions early. Firm C switched off every spreadsheet on go-live day. Staff reported that they had no way to check whether the system was right, so they built private copies, which then drifted away from the shared record. What did not matter as much as expected Training hours were similar across the three firms, and differences in the vendor's support were small. Feature gaps were mentioned often but rarely caused lasting problems; staff found simple workarounds. The decisive issues were about who owned the data and how people could check it. Discussion Our findings place information quality at the centre of small-firm ERP adoption, in line with DeLone and McLean (2003), and locate the critical moment in the shakedown phase…
